extraction.name: Common Corpus
extraction.description: Common Corpus is an open dataset of approximately two trillion tokens designed for language model pre-training. It consists entirely of uncopyrighted or permissively licensed data covering diverse domains, time periods, and multiple languages, serving as an open science infrastructure compliant with legal and AI regulatory requirements.
extraction.creator: Pierre-Carl Langlais, Carlos Rosas Hinostroza, Mattia Nee, Catherine Arnett, Pavel Chizhov, Eliot Krzystof Jones, Irène Girard, David Mach, Anastasia Stasenko, Ivan P. Yamshchikov
extraction.inLanguage: en, fr, de, es, la, it, pl, el, pt, ru, nl, lb, da, sv, sr, cs, ro, bg, lv, lt, hr, et, hu, sl, sk, ga, fi, mt, ar, bn, fa, sa, ur, mi, zh, ko
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was aggregated across six collections: Open Government (financial and legal data from public authorities like SEC, WTO, AMF, and legal databases), Open Culture (cultural heritage monographs and periodicals via Collections As Data dumps and APIs), Open Science (papers from OpenAlex, arXiv, and European repositories), Open Code (source code from The Stack v1 and v2), Open Web (Wikimedia Enterprise dumps, YouTube Commons transcripts, StackExchange via The Pile), and Open Semantic (Wikidata knowledge graph dumps).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Secondary Data analysis, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include SEC annual reports (EDGAR database), WTO Documents Online, AMF filings, TED EU Tenders, GATT Library, Europarl proceedings, Caselaw Access Project, CourtListener, EUR-lex, Eurovoc/Cellar, French DILA open data, USPTO patents, UN Digital Library, OECD datasets, Chronicling America, Europeana, Gallica (BnF), Biblioteca Digital Hispánica, Selected Digitized Books Collection, Delpher, Papers Past, German Digital Library, OpenAlex, arXiv, The Stack v1 and v2 (GitHub), Wikimedia dumps, YouTube transcripts, and Wikidata RDF dumps.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Wikidata RDF triples were adapted into simple natural language sequences without textual synthesis, providing consecutive translation blocks per entry separated by newlines. PII was identified and replaced with fictitious but realistic values to preserve text format. For Open Code, sequences of [\r]+\n were replaced with \n and line lengths were recalculated.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text segmentation was carried out using Segmentext. OCR quality assessment was performed using OCRoscope and OCRerrcr. OCR error correction was done using OCRonos. Personally Identifiable Information (PII) was detected using Microsoft Presidio enhanced with custom regular expressions and replaced with realistic fictitious data. Harmful and biased language was detected using the Celadon multilingual toxicity classifier, with flagged documents either removed or synthetically rewritten. Open Code underwent language/file format filtering (removing SVGs, data formats like csv/json/jsonld, and non-informative formats), license filtering to keep permissible licenses, removal of files with >=75% digits, and line length filtering.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Toxicity annotations were developed as part of a separate work (Arnett et al., 2024), where 2 million annotated samples across five dimensions (race and origin, gender and sexuality, religion, ability, and violence/abuse) were used to train the Celadon classifier.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Segmentext, OCRoscope, OCRerrcr, OCRonos, Presidio, Celadon, fastText
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Common Corpus is designed as an evolving, continuous research infrastructure rather than a fixed dataset. Hugging Face ensures proper archiving of past versions for reproducibility. Ongoing collection of European and African languages is planned under initiatives such as the LLMs4EU project.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) including phone numbers, email addresses, and IP addresses was identified and replaced with fictitious but realistic values.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Common Corpus provides a legally and ethically compliant foundation for pre-training open Large Language Models under stringent AI regulations (such as EU AI legislation and GDPR) without relying on fair use, preventing sudden takedowns, lowering hidden market externalities, and enabling reproducible, auditable open science.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Web-derived and user-generated data contain potential sexual content, hate speech, and demographic biases. Public domain historical texts (over 80 years old) contain outdated cultural norms, language, and stereotyping regarding ethnic groups, women, religion, ability, and violence.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset does not capture the entirety of open resources due to the open data paradox; coverage for low-resource languages (e.g., African languages) remains shallow; the corpus size of 2 trillion tokens is limited for training extremely large frontier models; automated curation tools (OCR correction, PII removal, toxicity filtering) do not attain 100% accuracy; and it does not contain instruction-tuning or task-specific fine-tuning data.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Pre-training of Large Language Models and Small Language Models; historical language modeling; development of vision-language models (VLMs) and document segmentation models; retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) training; creation of synthetic datasets, benchmarks, classifiers, and speech foundation models.
